title: GreenBoost serving recipe
description: NemoClaw audit, Phase 5a. GreenBoost-native (YAML instances validated against this JSON Schema) — a from-scratch schema following the IDEAS in NemoClaw's recipe.schema.json (digest-pinned model revision, a closed kvCache enum, a capabilities block with required keys pinned false until proven true) rather than a fork of its 1288 lines, which carry DGX/OpenShell-specific fields (gpu.count, containerRuntime) GreenBoost has no use for. A recipe turns gb_synapse.py's ctx/-ngl/KV-type heuristics into a validated document for models where the heuristic output has been measured and is worth pinning; a model with no recipe keeps using the heuristics unchanged (see gb_synapse.py's load_recipe()).

schemaVersion.description: Recipe schema version. Bump when a breaking shape change lands; check_recipes.py rejects a recipe whose schemaVersion this schema doesn't recognize.

name.description: gb_synapse manifest name this recipe applies to (matches ModelEntry.name).

revision.description: A real content-addressed revision (git SHA-1/SHA-256, or a sha256: digest) — NEVER a branch name or a mutable tag. Ported directly from NemoClaw's recipe.schema.json:58 pattern; the whole point of pinning a revision is that it can't silently move under the recipe.

sha256.description: Hex sha256 of this weight/config file, so a recipe can't silently drift onto a different file with the same path.

capabilities.description: Every key REQUIRED — a model can't silently claim a capability nothing checked for. toolCalls/streaming/mtpDraftHead are the ones GreenBoost's own reference workloads have actually exercised; visionProjector/recurrentState default to false (pinned in the schema below) until a recipe author has verified them the same way — the mechanism that would have caught the documented rope.dimension_sections and missing-mmproj incidents (CLAUDE.md's Reference Workload Rule section) as a validation failure instead of a load crash.

visionProjector.description: Pinned false — no GreenBoost reference workload has verified a vision projector through a recipe yet. Flip to a real boolean (drop the const) the day one is verified end-to-end, per-recipe.

recurrentState.description: Pinned false — same reasoning as visionProjector. A hybrid recurrent/attention model (n_recurrent_layers > 0) is real and supported by gb_synapse.py's estimate_ssm_state_gb(), but no recipe has yet been validated end-to-end claiming this capability; a model that needs it should still work through the heuristic (recipe-less) path today.

kvCache.description: Closed enum, not a free string — gb_synapse_backends.py passes these straight to llama.cpp's --cache-type-k/--cache-type-v with no validation today; this is the schema-side fix for that gap.

ctx.description: Context window this recipe was measured/validated at. Overrides gb_synapse.serve()'s heuristic ctx solve when this recipe is consumed.

nGpuLayers.description: -ngl. Either "all" (llama.cpp's -ngl 999 convention — every layer on GPU) or a non-negative integer layer count for a partial-offload recipe. Reaches LlamaCppBackend.serve()'s own -ngl decision directly via n_gpu_layers_override (NemoClaw audit, Phase 5/7 follow-up) — a value below entry.n_layers on a dense (non-MoE) model still clears the same _gate_cpu_offload() T2-spill safety check a live heuristic decision would.

mtpDraftN.description: --spec-draft-n-max override for an MTP-carrying model (only meaningful when capabilities.mtpDraftHead is true). Optional — omit for a model with no MTP head.

nCpuMoe.description: --n-cpu-moe override — measured, deliberate MoE-expert CPU placement (CLAUDE.md's 2026-07-26 amendment), never a silent fallback. Optional — omit for a dense model or a MoE model not using this placement.

kvReserveMb.description: GREENBOOST_KV_RESERVE_MB override — a real shim-observed measurement from gb_synapse.py's KV measurement cache (_persist_kv_measurement/_load_kv_measurement), promoted into a pinned recipe field. Optional — omit to let the measurement cache keep deriving it live.

tierIntent.description: Which tier-placement shape this recipe was measured under — t1Only (fits VRAM alone), t2Spill (host T2 DDR overflow, the shim's front-load split), or rpcSplit (llama.cpp --rpc across host+feeder). Informational + used by the Phase 7 preset resolver's requirements matching; gb_synapse.serve() does not yet branch on it directly (see load_recipe()'s docstring).

contentDigest.description: serving/digest.py's digest() of this recipe's own content with this field excluded — see serving/check_recipes.py. Detects any drift between a recipe's committed digest and its committed content.

sleepIdleSeconds.description: Seconds of idleness after which llama-server sleeps and releases VRAM (--sleep-idle-seconds). -1 disables. Exists because an idle session was measured holding 10.4 GiB of a 12 GB card at 0% utilization indefinitely.

specType.description: Speculative-decoding modes, in priority order, joined into llama.cpp's comma-separated --spec-type. ngram modes need no draft model and no extra VRAM. MEASURED per model, never assumed.

policy.description: Local-first enforcement, mirroring NemoClaw's managed-inference policy block. Makes CLAUDE.md's Local-First Must-Rule checkable rather than prose.

egress.description: Outbound network from the serving runtime.

modelSource.description: verified-local serves only what is already on disk, digest-checked.

modelDownloads.description: Whether a serve may fetch weights.

sampling.description: Sampling defaults the MODEL CARD specifies, passed to llama-server at launch. Exists because a model's published sampling values had no way to reach the engine: the recipe could pin ctx and KV type but not temperature, so a model whose card says top_k 20 / min_p 0.0 silently ran on llama.cpp's generic defaults (top_k 40 / min_p 0.05). A client that sends its own values per request still wins over these , these are defaults, not a ceiling.

source.description: Where these came from , a model-card URL, so a reader can check them rather than trust them.

kvCacheType.description: The three KV cache quantizations gb_synapse_backends.py actually passes to llama.cpp's --cache-type-k/-v today.
